**Gaps — no SOP yet**

- **Member Onboarding** – first 7 days critically shape retention; missing: induction checklist, goal-setting session structure, coach assignment logic, welcome communication sequence
- **Cancellation & Churn** – no documented win-back process or exit interview protocol; high-value members leaving without intervention
- **Member Checkins** – no cadence or framework for progress reviews; lost touchpoint for identifying churn risk and upselling
- **Coaching Development Roadmap** – no clear progression path for coaches; impacts quality consistency and staff retention
- **Class Quality Audit Checklist** – no systematic way to QA coaching delivery; risks inconsistent member experience
- **Member Pause** – no documented freeze/pause workflow; likely confusion on comms, duration rules, re-activation triggers
- **Referral Programme** – marketing spend may be wasted without clear mechanics and staff accountability
- **Member data privacy & GDPR** – legal and reputational risk; essential for gym data (photos, health info, comms consent)
- **Order Supplies & Sundries** – no inventory or reorder SOP; operational friction (towels, water, merchandise stock-outs)
- **Milestone Achievements** – no framework for celebrating wins; missed engagement and retention lever
- **Troubleshooting Guide** – members hit snags (app, class booking, billing); no escalation or resolution playbook

**Needs updating**

- **Existing Coaches SOPs (19/22)** – likely missing: session prep, form correction protocols, energy management mid-class, handling difficult members, post-class feedback loops
- **Clients SOPs (26/36)** – gaps probably in: complaint handling, refund/dispute process, membership tier upgrade/downgrade, payment failure workflow
- **Marketing SOPs (5/5)**

# Service Menu Execution for The Forge

**1. Start with your revenue breakdown, not your ego**
Pull last month's actual bookings: which services generate 80% of your income? Build the menu around those first. Add the aspirational stuff (monthly challenges, nutrition coaching) only if you have capacity. Grace, you're selling clarity—members buy what they understand instantly.

**2. Create two separate documents (not one confusing hybrid)**
- **Coach version**: Service name → time commitment → required expertise → pricing rationale (so they stop undercharging or dodging bookings)
- **Member version**: Service name → what you'll actually feel/see → price → how to book (remove all internal jargon—"metabolic conditioning" becomes "high-energy 45-min class")

**3. Price anchoring: Do this TODAY**
List every service. Next to each, write: lowest competitor price, your price, highest competitor price. If you're not in the middle-to-premium range, you're leaving money on the table. Use this to justify prices to coaches who'll question them.

**4. Embed "included" explicitly**
Don't assume people know. For each tier (group class vs. PT vs. membership), write: "Includes: locker access, water station, community chat group" etc. This prevents constant "is X included?" questions and upsells the actual value.

**5. Version control—today and quarterly**
Save this as "ServiceMenu_Jan2025_LIVE" in a shared folder. Set a quarterly review (don't wait for chaos). When coaches say "but can we add..." you have a process, not a debate.
